hook: David Sacks is a Silicon Valley entrepreneur and venture capitalist who spent over 25 years building and investing in technology companies before taking on a formal role in AI and crypto policy. Born in South Africa, he came up in Silicon Valley as PayPal's first product leader and chief operating officer, then founded the enterprise social network Yammer, which Microsoft acquired for 1.2 billion dollars in 2012. He went on to found Craft Ventures, a San Francisco venture capital firm, and became an early investor in companies including Airbnb, SpaceX and Palantir, while co-hosting the widely followed All-In podcast. In December 2024, President-elect Trump named him White House AI and Crypto Czar, a newly created post directing administration policy on artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency and chairing the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. After roughly 130 days in that day-to-day role, he stepped down in March 2026 and was named co-chair of PCAST alongside OSTP Director Michael Kratsios, broadening his advisory portfolio to the wider range of federal science and technology policy.
